body.objective: Students will be able to count to 100.
successCriteria: I can count from 0 to 100 in Mandarin
I can read and write number characters
I can use numbers in phone numbers, math and prices
body.hook: Mandarin numbers are among the most logical in the world: 11 is "ten-one," 20 is "two-ten," 99 is "nine-ten-nine." Learn 1–10 and you can count to 99 instantly.

study.title: 数字
study.question: How do numbers work in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Numbers (written for this lesson):
一 yī, 二 èr, 三 sān, 四 sì, 五 wǔ, 六 liù, 七 qī, 八 bā, 九 jiǔ, 十 shí, 零 líng (zero).
11–19: 十 + number: 十一 shíyī (11), 十五 shíwǔ (15).
Tens: number + 十: 二十 èrshí (20), 五十 wǔshí (50).
21–99: tens + ones: 二十一 èrshíyī (21), 九十九 jiǔshíjiǔ (99).
100: 一百 yìbǎi.
两 liǎng is used for "two" before measure words: 两个人 (two people).
Phone numbers: digits read one by one; 一 is often said yāo to avoid confusion with 七 qī.
Math: 三加四等于七 sān jiā sì děngyú qī (3 + 4 = 7).
Culture: 八 bā sounds like 发 fā (to prosper), so 8 is considered lucky; 四 sì sounds like 死 sǐ (death), so 4 is often avoided in building floor numbers.
Finger counting: there are one-hand signs for 6–10 (e.g. 6 = thumb and pinkie out).
Activities: number bingo, math races and phone-number dictation.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson; number cultural notes are widely described.
discussion: When do you use 两 instead of 二?
How do you say 1 in phone numbers?

body.objective: Students will be able to say the date.
successCriteria: I can say and write dates in Mandarin
I can say months and my birthday
I can ask what the date is
body.hook: In Mandarin, dates go from biggest to smallest: year, month, day, like 2026年11月3日. Once you know numbers, dates are easy, because months are just numbered.

vocabulary.term: 几月几号? jǐ yuè jǐ hào

study.title: 几月几号?
study.question: How do I say dates in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Dates (written for this lesson):
Order: year → month → day: 2026年11月3日 (èr líng èr liù nián shíyī yuè sān rì).
Years: read digit by digit: 2026 = 二零二六年 èr líng èr liù nián.
Months: number + 月: 一月 (January), 二月 (February), … 十二月 (December).
Days: number + 日 (written) or 号 (spoken): 三号.
Questions: 今天几月几号? Jīntiān jǐ yuè jǐ hào? (What's the date today?) 你的生日是几月几号? Nǐ de shēngrì shì jǐ yuè jǐ hào? (When is your birthday?)
Answers: 今天十一月三号。我的生日是五月二十号。
Culture: many families also celebrate the Lunar New Year, whose date changes each year in January or February because it follows the lunar calendar. A traditional birthday food is long noodles (长寿面 chángshòu miàn) for long life.
Activity: birthday line-up: students line up in birthday order by asking 你的生日是几月几号? in Mandarin only.
study.source: Original activity written for this lesson.

body.objective: Students will be able to say days of the week.
body.iCan: I can say days of the week.
successCriteria: I can say the days of the week in Mandarin
I can ask and say what day it is
I can describe my weekly schedule
body.hook: Monday in Mandarin is literally "week-one": 星期一. The days are numbered, except Sunday, which is "week-sun" or "week-heaven." It's one of the easiest systems to learn.

vocabulary.term: 星期天 / 星期日 xīngqītiān / xīngqīrì
今天星期几? jīntiān xīngqī jǐ

study.title: 星期几?
study.question: How do I say the days of the week in Mandarin?
study.passage:
Days (written for this lesson):
星期一 Monday, 星期二 Tuesday, 星期三 Wednesday, 星期四 Thursday, 星期五 Friday, 星期六 Saturday, 星期天 or 星期日 Sunday.
Pattern: 星期 + number (1–6); Sunday uses 天 (sky/day) or 日 (sun).
Also common: 周一 zhōuyī, 周二… (shorter, often in writing and schedules).
Question: 今天星期几? Answer: 今天星期二。
Full date with day: 今天是2026年11月3日, 星期二。
Schedule sentences (time words go before the verb): 我星期一有中文课。Wǒ xīngqīyī yǒu Zhōngwén kè. (I have Chinese class on Monday.) 星期六我踢足球。Xīngqīliù wǒ tī zúqiú. (On Saturday I play soccer.) 周末我看电影。Zhōumò wǒ kàn diànyǐng. (On the weekend I watch movies.)
Activity: make a weekly planner in characters; partners ask 你星期几有…? and answer.
